meta.purpose: The 100k-archive red-probe series behind the numbers cited in migration 01.00.21_01, src/taskq/web/admin/jobs.py's UNION-shape comment, and tests/test_scan_budget.py's docstrings. Measured during the scale campaign on PostgreSQL 18.6 (timescale/timescaledb:2.30.1-pg18 image run vanilla), a 100,000-row jobs_archive seeded by the campaign's seed shape, the admin page statement built by taskq.web.admin.jobs._build_paginated_sql verbatim, EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, FORMAT JSON). The 10M-scale series these legs extend is benchmarks/results/archive-scale.json (pagination_pathology).

page1_unserved_ordering.what: page 1 (no cursor) of the archive tab on the SHIPPED indexes (pre-01.00.21_01): the finished_at DESC NULLS LAST, id DESC ordering is matched by no index, so the plan is a full sort of the matching population

cursor_page_or_wrapped_predicate.what: a value-cursor page (~150d deep) with the page index present, before the builder's UNION split: the keyset predicate rendered (finished_at IS NULL OR row-compare); the OR defeats index-condition extraction
cursor_page_or_wrapped_predicate.filter: (((finished_at IS NULL) OR (ROW(finished_at, id) < ROW($2, $3))) AND (status = ANY(...)))
cursor_page_or_wrapped_predicate.note: the scan runs from the index start and filters; page cost linear in walked depth

cursor_page_union_shape.what: the same page after the builder's UNION split: two ordered index branches (values seek + NULL-range seek) under a Merge Append

row_wise_index_cond_proof.what: the bare row-wise compare (no OR wrapper) extracts as an Index Cond and seeks: the A/B that isolates the OR as the blocker

walk_row_exactness.what: the UNION shape walked 5,049 rows over 99 pages (seed with NULL finished_at rows present) and matched a reference ORDER BY finished_at DESC NULLS LAST, id DESC walk exactly; page p50 0.30 ms, p95 0.90 ms
